decisions.summary: Fix the flake at its cause in the test fixture: World::new's in-process std::fs::copy of the template is replaced by one `cp -a <template>/. <world>` child, so no descriptor of the test process writes a world's fakes and no fork can inherit one. The why and a 'do not copy in-process again' sit at copy, and the module header is corrected.
decisions.why: T263's line as relayed in the block (find the race, make the test deterministic, fix the cause and not a retry) asks for exactly this. It removes the cause rather than retrying, and covers every fake the template carries at once.

decisions.summary: The cause is attributed to ETXTBSY from a descriptor inherited across another thread's fork during the fixture's copy. 451 T258's state restore is excluded because the fixture runs a three-line fake sync. The failing notice is reconstructed by forcing, not recovered from the red gate.
decisions.why: This is a finding, not a scope choice. The block itself says the attribution rests on a forced reproduction and a fixture read rather than recovered output, and the first-assertion print hedges a misattribution. Whether the mechanism is right is a design and correctness question, not a fidelity one.

decisions.summary: The first assertion prints the notice it read ("{full}"), so a future failure shows what was said.
decisions.why: It serves 'find the race' for any recurrence. The test checks the same thing and only says more when it fails.

decisions.summary: The guard's code is not changed. A refresh that cannot START its script still says `mirror refresh FAILED: ` with nothing after the colon.
decisions.why: Measured against the wrong-outcome definition (constitution XIV v2.36.0), this is not a defect. The notice says truthfully that the refresh failed, it is said in full every time, and it is the same branch a failing script takes. In a real clone the script is a git-written file that this process never holds open, so the cause cannot occur there. A sparser message than one might like is a difference, not a wrong outcome, so leaving it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: No kept test forces the race. The red-first was a one-shot stub on the unfixed copy: a sleep-3 child handed the copied script's write handle. It gave 520 passed and 1 failed at this test's first assertion, then 521 passed with the stub removed and 521 passed with the fix.
decisions.why: The relayed task line asks for red-first by forcing the interleaving, and the forced red answers that. Nothing in the GM's request or the task line asks for a kept regression pin of this race, so leaving it out narrows nothing that was asked. The plan's impossibility argument covers a behavioural pin only, since the fixed copy holds no descriptor to race. A structural pin, such as a lint on in-process copies in the fixture, would be possible, but it is not required by anything asked.

decisions.summary: The sibling census of ways a rust/guard test could directly run a file its own process wrote names its forms (from_mode, set_permissions, 0o literals, .mode(0o, chmod children, fs::copy, and fs::write/File::create/OpenOptions on .sh or scripts/bin/hooks paths), reads every hit, and finds no other instance. Crates outside rust/guard were not searched.
decisions.why: The search space is stated with its method, as FR-009 and the enumeration rule require. The boundary is drawn openly at this guard's crate, which is where the task lies, and no known defect is carried forward, so it is not a narrowing under the fix-as-we-go rule.

decisions.summary: Order: any time, nothing waits on it. Budget: one landing. Performance work: no. Exits: closing-checks green, or red recorded and ruled through arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The only GM words that bear on these are the 2026-11-20 performance-first order and the 2026-11-22 bundling note, and neither is narrowed. Classing a flake fix as non-performance leaves FR-013's ordering to apply to it as the GM set it.

### T263 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The flake's cause is the fixture's in-process std::fs::copy of the fake scripts (a forked child inherits the write descriptor, exec gives ETXTBSY), not 451 T258's state restore; the empty-reason notice is reconstructed by forcing, not recovered.
decisions.why: Finding the cause is what T263's line asks. The block labels the reconstruction as such and names the other mechanism that would give the same notice (a refused fork). Its reason for picking the descriptor race is that this fixture makes it possible and its neighbors do not. The forced red reproduces exactly this assertion's failure.

decisions.summary: copy() becomes one `cp -a <template>/. <world>` child, covering all four fakes at once, with its why and a 'do not copy in-process again' beside it.
decisions.why: This fixes the cause rather than adding a retry, which is what the brief asks. Which mechanism to use is a design choice, not a fidelity question.

decisions.summary: The first assertion prints the notice it read ("{full}").
decisions.why: It serves the task's goal that a red first assertion shows what was said. It only makes a failure readable and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: No kept test forces the race; red-first was a scratch stub in the unfixed copy (520 passed, 1 failed, then 521 passed with the fix).
decisions.why: T263's line asks for red-first by forcing the interleaving, and item 9 records that forcing with its command and result. Once the fixed copy is in place there is no descriptor left to hand a child, so a kept test of the race would be testing the kernel. FR-012's kept red-first tests cover FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013's refusals, and this fixture is none of them.

decisions.summary: The guard is unchanged; a refresh that cannot start its script still says 'mirror refresh FAILED: ' with nothing after it; 'Found and left? none'.
decisions.why: By the defect rule this is not a wrong outcome. The notice correctly says the refresh failed, says so every time, and takes the same branch as a failing script. A missing reason after the colon is a diagnostic gap, not a wrong answer. Leaving it is therefore within what was asked, and 'Found and left? none' does not hide a defect.

decisions.summary: The class (a file the test process writes, then execs, while other test threads fork) is declared to have no other instance, on a census of `set_permissions`, `0o755` and `fs::copy` under rust/guard, and the step table states 'a world's scripts are written by no descriptor of the test process'.
decisions.why: The block names a class of defect: the hazard write_executable already names, and the fixture's copy 'outside it'. FR-009 therefore requires a line saying how every instance was found, and the census's method cannot see one form of the class. A test that rewrites a world's script in-process after the copy (fs::write, File::create or OpenOptions over a path cp -a has already made executable) needs no set_permissions, no 0o755 and no fs::copy, so the grep is blind to it. Such a rewrite recreates the same race, in this fixture's own tests or elsewhere under rust/guard. A mode other than the literal 0o755 (0o700, 0o775, 0o777) is also missed. Nothing makes the narrower census necessary: it is not impossible, not implied by any GM words, and the full search does not defeat the task's purpose. It IS the purpose, since a missed instance leaves the landing gate flaky. This ruling does not assert that such an instance exists. FIX: either widen the Siblings line to cover in-process writes (fs::write, File::create, OpenOptions, any 0o7 mode or from_mode) to any path a test later runs, at least across the guard crate's test fixtures, and state the result as an observation with its method; or cut the claim back to what the method saw, i.e. 'no test writes a file it marks executable with 0o755 or copies one with fs::copy'. Either is followed by fixing any instance found.

decisions.summary: T301's section is PART 1 of four (the measurement of why one target directory holds 20 to 31 hashes of a crate); no code changed, parts 2-4 (eviction, the scratch sweep's patterns, loose profraw files) left to later builders and the task left unticked.
decisions.why: The task line divides T301 into four parts and this section claims only the first; the task stays open, so nothing of what was asked is dropped, only ordered. Measuring before sweeping serves the GM's 2026-11-22 words on cleaning up after ourselves while reusing the same build cache.

decisions.summary: Nothing deleted; the session clone's cache only read; every build in the pool tree diagram-backlog-t271's own target.
decisions.why: A measurement that changes no cache is the conservative form of part 1 and narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: The finding: no setting flips between the gate's cargo calls (unchanged re-runs all Fresh); the hashes are live build configurations, past profile values (451 T246's debug = 0) and dependency-feature siblings; the GM's question on a builder's repeated test runs is answered (a run that changes nothing compiles nothing, one changed crate 2 to 4 s; about 19 s is a first plain build in a tree that never built it, or the tests' own run time, m9-results 14.6 to 23.8 s).
decisions.why: This is the answer to the question the GM asked on 2026-11-26 (451 T315's line: 'more of the compilation was not able to be cached') and to T301's task line, each figure dated with its method.

decisions.summary: Found and left: a crate below a testkit crate is compiled once per feature combination the selected packages ask for (17 of 75 rustc runs after a touch of core), and rust/Cargo.toml's ONE FEATURE SET comment holds for outside crates only. Not fixed here: a choice between two forms that each need measuring, touching kept.rs, side.rs and cover.rs; filed as T325 [perf], lands before T278.
decisions.why: A deferral in exactly the form the accepted spec provides (FR-009, D15: why, the filed id, the order), to a [perf] task that FR-013 schedules ahead of other work, ordered before the variant sweep that would otherwise keep the sibling hashes. The measurement task's part 1 is not asked to carry a design change between two unmeasured forms; nothing is dropped. The comment's correction rides with T325, which changes the behavior it describes.

decisions.summary: Found and left: a pool tree handed out warm compiles from nothing each configuration its earlier tasks never built (58 first builds, 246 s for all 28 gate manifests' plain test builds). Judged not a defect and not filed.
decisions.why: Nothing is built twice and the builds are kept; the cost is paid once per tree and crate. That is no wrong outcome under constitution XIV v2.36.0 (no crash, hang, refusal or wrong answer, no check passing bad work), and it is recorded as one reading of the test runs the GM asked about. Leaving a non-defect as it is stays within.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no: a measurement; what it found to make faster is T325's, a [perf] task.'
decisions.why: The plan rules T301 out of performance work on the ground 'no: a measurement' - the one ground FR-013 and the GM remove: 'I would also like for this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first. Because it's so closely related to performance that it should be counted as such even if the task itself doesn't improve performance.' (2026-11-20). Part 1 measures whether the gate's builds recompile needlessly and answers the GM's question of 2026-11-26 on why a builder's test runs could not reuse more compilation, and it files a compile-time cost: it is work that measures where the time goes. None of the three grounds holds: counting it is not impossible, the GM's words imply the opposite, and counting it defeats nothing (that part 1 has already run is no ground). Fix: the line says part 1 is performance work for ordering under FR-013's measurement clause; if parts 2 to 4 (eviction, the scratch sweep, the profraw files) are to stay unprioritized, it says so of those parts, citing the GM's words that put disk work later. Those words are not in request.md; the block cites only the task line's restatement. Cause worth fixing: the section template's 'Performance work?' prompt defines [perf] as 'makes ... faster' and leaves out FR-013's measurement clause.

decisions.summary: Part B for the batch whose gate was red twice on unreached lines (sections.rs 55, builder_done.rs 327, then words.rs 143): one line's error made eager with ok_or in place of ok_or_else's closure, the same behavior, no test weakened; the batch gate run once more with nothing else carried in, under the round arbiter's continue ruling.
decisions.why: A coverage repair that keeps behavior and weakens no test, followed by the arbiter's ruled next step. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Under the two tiers a builder runs no coverage, so a few coverage failures fixed at the batch gate are the accepted cost.
decisions.why: This is the GM's own two-tier direction of 2026-11-26 (request.md, 451 T308: full rigor deferred until the session clone goes through its gates).

decisions.summary: After the ruling: a red on the load-sensitive hook-suite case alone (451 T139) is re-run as that suite and not counted a third red; a new unreached line is fixed the same way and asked again.
decisions.why: The suite must still pass on its re-run, so nothing lands on a red and no test is waived. The open fix of the load-sensitive case (the GM, 2026-11-26: 'I agree with prioritizing the test that fails under load being fixed') is untouched. It concerns the arbiter's red count, which no clause of the request sets.

decisions.summary: T301's 'Performance work?' now answers yes for part 1: a measurement task, counted as performance work for ordering by the GM's words of 2026-11-20 (it makes nothing faster itself; T325 is the [perf] fix it found).
decisions.why: FR-013 and request.md line 46 ('this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first'). Round 1's BLOCKED item T301-not-perf said 'no: a measurement', which contradicted this; the new line states it as the request does. Resolved.

decisions.summary: T301 parts 2 to 4 (what to evict, the scratch sweep's patterns, the loose profraw files) are disk work, begun after the talk on parallelizing and ordered by time saved, never by disk freed.
decisions.why: request.md '2026-11-26: the disk work and the principle behind it', verbatim GM words: 'the guiding principle is still time saved is more important than disk usage ... we definitely don't want to clean things up if it is going to cost us time later' and 'fix all of this as part of our tasking ... before resuming our port. But after we talk about the most efficient way to parallelize.' Disk eviction makes nothing faster, so it is not FR-013 performance work and putting it after the parallelizing talk follows the GM's own order. Ordering it by time saved applies his stated principle rather than narrowing it. Nothing is dropped: the parts stay open and the task stays unticked.
